title.narrative: CCASE_Research and Advocacy on Non-Economic aspects of Loss & Damage due to climate change

description.narrative: The International Centre for Climate Change and Development (ICCCAD) based at the Independent University, Bangladesh (IUB) was created in 2009 and has already established itself as a leading centre for conducting state of the art research and providing training and capacity building, on tackling climate change, to government and non-government actors in least developed countries (LDCs). It is a leading research institute, based in Bangladesh, working on climate change related issues, not limited to the national context, but also conducting research and advocacy globally. ICCCAD’s Loss and Damage Programme is based on 3 main pillars which include Research, Capacity Building and Advocacy activities. ICCCAD’s Loss & Damage Research portfolio predominantly focuses on non-economic loss and damage (NELD), which we now frame as Value Based Loss & Damage (VBLnD). This allows us to go beyond a normative understanding of climate impacts and varies across different communities and geographic location. Through this concept, we aim to explore what the affected communities value most and how they can respond to the impacts accordingly. ICCCAD is going to implement a project titled ‘Evidence based approach to Address Non-Economic aspects of losses and damages (EBAN)’. Objectives of the Project The project’s general objective is to understand and address the knowledge and capacity gaps of two climatic hotspots in Bangladesh so that an informed NELD response and implementation mechanism can be developed at the country level. Five specific objectives include: 1. To generate new evidence on non economics losses and damages, from local level 2. To strengthen the understanding of NELD through diagnostic assessment of NELD (by creating needs assessment and response framework) 3. To facilitate novel methodologies of measuring losses and damages through Value based approach 4. To provide training and capacity building opportunities to Local and National stakeholders 5. To disseminate this knowledge to global actors and Negotiators help them formulate coherent approach to L&D negotiation within UNFCCC system
